speaker_role: independent counselor (Ethan, 'College Essay Guy'; former alumni interviewer for Northwestern, no longer does interview prep himself)
commercial_incentive: yes - promotes his site (collegeessayguy.com) and a downloadable 'ultimate guide' of interview questions, though the video's core content is free
key_insights: Cites NACAC's annual survey showing the interview ranks near the bottom of factors colleges say they weigh, though a cited Babson admissions officer and an Atlantic article debate how much interviews really matter.
Recommends checking a school's Common Data Set section C7 (or emailing the admissions office) to see whether that specific school actually rates the interview as a factor.
Distinguishes informational interviews (just a conversation/Q&A) from evaluative ones (assessed for fit), and says to find out which type you're getting beforehand.
Says declining an optional interview can hurt because many schools track 'demonstrated interest,' and simply completing the interview may matter more than how polished it was.
Advises writing three prep documents beforehand: a 'why this school' answer, a 'what do you want to major in and why' answer, and a paragraph on non-academic interests.

Teaches a 'message box' technique: pre-select 3-4 talking points you want to work into answers regardless of the question asked, built via a '21 random details about yourself' brainstorm plus asking friends/family what stands out about you.

Recommends the 'so what?' game to practice turning simple answers into reflective, specific stories, and to prepare 1-3 specific, non-googleable questions to ask the interviewer to demonstrate research and create personal connection.

Practical logistics tips: dress a notch nicer than a t-shirt, avoid strong cologne/perfume for in-person interviews, check lighting/software for virtual interviews, and it's fine to pause or say 'I don't know' rather than force an awkward answer.
specific_numbers_or_facts: NACAC's annual survey of colleges reportedly ranks the interview near the bottom of factors considered in admissions (per the video, exact ranking not shown in transcript).
The '21 details exercise': write 21 random facts about yourself on paper as raw material for the message box.
Message box should contain 3-4 core talking points to weave into interview answers.
notable_or_distinctive: The concrete, reusable frameworks (message box, 21-details exercise, 'so what?' game) and the tip to look up a school's Common Data Set section C7 to gauge real interview weight are unusually actionable rather than generic platitudes.
reliability_notes: Advice is from an independent counselor/content creator, not a named current admissions officer, and cites the NACAC survey and Atlantic article only loosely (no specific numbers shown in transcript); the video also funnels viewers to his paid/lead-gen content.
